content.value: PDS Wave 22 — Success Must Be Observable: the unattended-owner wave

Living wave Paper for wave 22 of the Personal Development Server epic (epic task task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md, read from origin/main @ fe1e4501a (4,134 lines). Prior wave Paper: pds-wave-21-2026-07-21 — the crown SEALED 12/12, grade A-. Every later phase appends here; someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where the wave stands.

Phase: STRATEGIZE complete, 17 broad surveyors about to fly. The crown is CLOSED and will not be re-fired. This wave's whole worth: the PDS proved the loop CAN fire once, watched, on a hand-armed ladder. It did not prove the product is trustworthy in an owner's hands unattended. The gap between those two is a single defect class — surfaces that REPORT SUCCESS WHILE BEING WRONG — and this wave closes it.
The Wish

Close the gap between "the dev loop fired once, supervised" and "an owner can trust this box unattended." The epic carries ~130 open rows; the ones that matter are correctness defects where the system reported success while being wrong — the exact failure class the crown ladder was built to catch, and the exact class an unattended owner cannot catch for themselves. Four named starting points, to be RE-DERIVED and not trusted: pds-bl-deploy-success-without-advance, pds-bl-scratch-pointer-concurrency, pds-bl-close-holder-and-criteria-gate, pds-bl-streaming-workspace-export. Plus: triage the ~130 rows the way Truth-Grip wave 10 triaged its tail — adjudicate by CONTENT against main, close what is already fixed, park what is genuinely deferred WITH a durable reason, leave the rest open with a named owner. Do NOT re-fire the crown. Do NOT invent a new capability to avoid finishing the ones that exist.
The Direction — SUCCESS MUST BE OBSERVABLE
One law, proposed for the charter, and every slice is an instance of it:

No Barkpark verb may report success on an exit code alone. Every success claim must be backed by a post-condition READ of the state it claims to have produced — and any claim it cannot back must say so in the same breath. A green that cannot fail is not a green.

This is the repo's own agent doctrine — distrust vacuous green, verify STATE not exit codes, truth-authority level 1 is the running system — made EXECUTABLE IN THE PRODUCT rather than practised only by agents. That is exactly what separates a watched dev loop from an unattended one: a supervising lead re-derives every claim by hand; an owner cannot, so the box must do it, and must be loud when it cannot.

What the finished experience feels like. The owner deploys and the thing that says SUCCESS is the box's own advanced HEAD, not a CI conclusion. A close on the ledger means the worker who held the claim finished the criteria — or it says out loud, on the record, that it did not. An import receipt prints the rows it actually moved, not an em-dash. A second concurrent scratch target cannot silently strand the first. An export route refuses work it cannot serve instead of dying trying. Nothing new is invented: four or five existing surfaces stop lying.
What the ground truth already changed
Premise smoke, run against origin/main @ fe1e4501a BEFORE any direction was committed. Three of the wish's own premises moved:
pds-bl-streaming-workspace-export — the export accumulates a live dumps map and File.read!s the tar back as a second full-size binary

STALE. Wave 11's spill (PDS-D207) already made packing FILE-TO-FILE and constant-memory; archive.ex's own moduledoc says so, and workspace_controller.ex:178 already send_file/3s the tar. The EXPORT half is DONE on main.

Re-scope. The live half is IMPORT — Archive.unpack still materialises the whole bundle into a dumps map (PDS-D214 left it deliberately unchanged) — plus the unbounded import body read, plus an export route that still has NO server-side serialization.
An orphaned fire worktree at /Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark-w21-fire to be pruned
ALREADY ABSENT. ls returns No such file or directory, and it appears in no git worktree list entry (1,459 worktrees enumerated).
Housekeeping closes on evidence. Nothing to prune, and git worktree prune is never run.
pds-bl-close-holder-and-criteria-gate — close enforces only the epoch
CONFIRMED LIVE. api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex check_fencing/2 matches content.claim.epoch and nothing else; worker identity is never compared, and no criterion state gates a done close.
Real — and it is the ledger's own success claim, the primitive every other wave's evidence rests on.

The first row is the argument for the triage track in miniature: one of the four named starting points was already fixed by a prior wave, and the ledger did not know. Triage here is not bookkeeping. It is what stops this wave rebuilding what main already has.
The Direction Debate
Three candidates were developed far enough to be attacked.
A — SUCCESS MUST BE OBSERVABLE (WINNER)

Fix the success-lies in the PDS loop: deploy advance, task-close holder + criteria, import and receipt honesty, scratch-pointer concurrency, import-side streaming and export serialization. Plus the full triage. One charter law binds them.

WON. It states the wish's defect class as an INVARIANT rather than a list, so it generalises past the four named rows; every slice finishes something that already exists; and it is the precondition for any later owner-facing self-check.
B — THE UNATTENDED OWNER RUN
Productise the 4,134-line hand-armed crown ladder into a one-verb bp dev verify the owner runs unattended — the Kinsta/Vercel-shaped answer, a status surface that proves the box is what it claims.

LOST on two counts. It invents a new capability to avoid finishing the ones that exist, which the wish forbids outright. And fatally: a self-check built on lying primitives INHERITS the lie — it would read the same CI conclusion, the same epoch-only close, the same em-dash receipt, and report green. B is a strong wave-23 candidate that A must precede.
C — THE HONEST LEDGER
Narrow: fix bp task close, then spend the rest of the wave on the 130-row triage.
LOST as a whole wave — it is a proper subset of A, and a wave whose only build is one CAS gate under-spends a fleet. Fully absorbed: C is A's first slice and A's second track.
The sharpest attack found on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it:

A strict holder fence on bp task close would break the epic-cycle's own workflow. The charter says in plain text "PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge)", and wave 21 was sealed by a LEAD closing a builder's task. Two other waves and ~110 agents are on the ledger RIGHT NOW, some on older CLI builds. A criteria gate would additionally refuse legitimate closes — cancelled rows, and criteria the charter itself marks unmeasurable by design (pds-bl-reclimb-criterion4-unmeasurable-by-design). Shipped naively, this slice is an outage.

blocks.title: ATTACK — the close gate can break the fleet that is running it

content.value: ABSORPTION, and it makes the slice better rather than smaller: the gate is LOUD, not CLOSED. A holder mismatch does not refuse — it demands an explicit, recorded override (a named actor and a reason written into the close event), so a lead close stays legal and becomes AUDITABLE for the first time. A done close with unmet criteria likewise requires an explicit accept-unmet carrying a reason, while cancelled and blocked lifecycles are untouched. And the default-on question is not settled by taste: a surveyor MEASURES how many real closes in the live task.closed event history had worker != holder before anything is gated. That is survey assignment 1, and it is the wave's single highest-leverage unknown.

Two lesser attacks and their answers. (1) "Triaging 130 rows is bureaucracy that fixes nothing." The streaming-export finding above already refutes it; and triage is surveyor and verifier fan-out — cheap, parallel — while builders spend only on defects. Every row must land in exactly one of: CLOSED with the commit that fixed it, PARKED with a durable reason and a named reopen trigger, or OPEN with a named owner and a size. (2) "Deploy honesty lives in .github/workflows, which is fenced to the concurrent Honest Gates wave." Correct, and the fence is respected — the honest fix belongs on the BOX side anyway, because the box's own advanced HEAD is the fact and a CI conclusion is at best hearsay. It lands in deploy/instance-deploy.sh plus a read path, never in the workflow file.
Priorities for this wave
Ledger close honesty — holder + criteria, loud recorded override, measured before it is gated
It is the primitive every other wave's evidence rests on. If close can lie, every green in this repo is unaudited.
Deploy advance honesty — box-side, with a read path, never .github/workflows
The unattended owner's single most consequential question is "is the box running what I merged?" Today, success does not imply advance.
THE TRIAGE — every open row adjudicated by content against main
Largest open backlog on the board, and already proven stale in at least one place. Shrinking it HONESTLY is a first-class deliverable, not cleanup.
Receipt and report honesty cluster — import counts, blob byte verify, counts perspective, flat-verb -w, manifest writes fails-open
Small, cheap, and each one is literally the owner being told something untrue.
Import-side streaming plus export-route serialization
Re-scoped by smoke: the export half landed. What remains is the import materialisation, the unbounded body read, and a route that accepts work it cannot serve.
Scratch-target pointer concurrency
Two concurrent targets clobber through one global pointer; the crown waves lost real time to exactly this class.
Charter-assigned housekeeping

Close pds-w21-diagnose-and-fire (criterion 6 met by #5547, merge 59818468e) and pds-w21-crown-collect-and-seal (the seal fulfilled it). The worktree is already gone — record the evidence and touch nothing.

No crown re-fire. Fable is unavailable (spend limit) — every joint runs Opus, and no dispatch may select fable. Keep off .github/workflows/** and the hg-* ledger namespace (concurrent Honest Gates wave) and tooling/grip/** (Truth-Grip refire); collision control is atomic bp claims. Main carries two standing reds — Format (advisory) and Sobelow — that are NOT ours. Guerrilla writes are degraded to 15-33s under concurrent load: NEVER conclude a ledger write failed without RE-READING the published state, which is, fittingly, this wave's own law applied to itself.
The Survey Plan — 17 assignments
Width now buys precise depth later. Each assignment is one Opus surveyor at medium effort. Every load-bearing assumption the stress-test surfaced appears below as a question.
close-holder-blast-radius

In the LIVE task.closed event history on guerrilla, how many closes had a closing worker different from the claim holder, and who were they — a lead, the epic-cycle harness, the board UI, the CI autostamp? Read api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex, claim.ex, the tasks_controller close action, board_live.ex:454-475, and every caller of Tasks.close across api/, internal/, tooling/ and .claude/workflows/.

THE decisive unknown. It decides whether the holder gate can default on, must default to warn-only, or needs a recorded-override path from day one. Shipped wrong, it is an outage for two concurrent waves.
criteria-gate-semantics

What fraction of already-done PDS tasks would have been REFUSED by an unmet-criteria gate on a done close? Enumerate the legitimate exceptions the charter itself creates — merge-gated criteria closed by the lead, criteria marked unmeasurable by design, cancelled and blocked lifecycles — and find how criteria.ex and the stamp path represent met.
Sets the exact shape of the gate: which lifecycles it covers, what the override records, and whether it can ever be retroactive.
deploy-advance-truth

Map EVERY path by which the deploy workflow concludes success without guerrilla's HEAD advancing: the skipped instance job when changes.outputs.instance is false, the coalesce no-op at instance-deploy.sh:311-313, the lock-held exit 23, a failed slot flip. Then: where does the box record what it is ACTUALLY running (.instance-deploy-last, slot state, the Caddy upstream port), and is there any read path a non-SSH observer can use today?
Defines the box-side fix and the read path while staying entirely out of .github/workflows/**, which is fenced to the Honest Gates wave.
success-claim-census

Sweep the PDS surfaces — internal/cli/cloud_workspace_cmd.go, the workspace controller export/import actions, scripts/pds-*.sh, bin/barkpark, deploy/*.sh — for every place a SUCCESS, PASS or exit-0 is printed. For each, name whether a post-condition read of the claimed state backs it, or whether it is an exit code wearing a green hat.
Turns the direction's law from a slogan into a ranked list of real sites, and will surface lies nobody has filed yet.
triage-corpus

Enumerate EVERY open descendant row of task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5. The tree is deeper than one level: 81 direct open children were counted, but the lead measured ~130 open descendants. For each row report doc_id, title, priority, criteria count, claim state, and the files it names. Then cluster them into families.
The triage track cannot start without an accurate corpus, and the count itself is currently in dispute (81 vs 130).
triage-already-fixed

Adjudicate 30 open rows by CONTENT against origin/main: does the defect still reproduce in the code as written today? For every already-fixed row, name the commit or PR that fixed it. Start with the harness-bug family — pgrep sampler, step-1 grain control, gate-b anticorrelated, artdir cleanup, deployed-sha override, step-6 controls — and the streaming/import family.
The streaming-export premise was already stale. This measures how widespread that is, and it is the single biggest lever on shrinking the blocking set honestly.
streaming-import-half

Re-derive the streaming state end to end. Confirm PDS-D207's spill plus send_file on the EXPORT side, then map exactly what remains on the IMPORT side: Archive.unpack materialising the bundle, the dumps map in run_import, the unbounded request body read in the import action, and whether the export route has ANY server-side serialization or concurrency gate (PDS-D31 is a client-side policy only).
Re-scopes one of the four named starting points and decides whether the remaining work is one slice or three.
scratch-pointer-concurrency

Read scripts/pds-scratch-target.sh in full. What exactly breaks when two up calls share the default pointer /tmp/pds-scratch-target.last — stranded roots, a teardown aimed at the wrong target, the PORT-defaults-to-4000 hazard in bin/barkpark stop? What is the minimal default that is safe without breaking the documented pinned-pointer recipe?
Three open rows (pds-bl-scratch-pointer-concurrency, pds-bl-scratch-pointer-explicit-default, pds-barkpark-stop-4000-fallback) may be one slice; this decides.
receipt-honesty-cluster

For each of pds-bl-import-receipt-counts (the CLI decoding the server's tables MAP as an int, printing em-dashes), pds-bl-blob-sidecar-byte-verify, pds-bl-counts-perspective-honesty, pds-backlog-flat-verb-workspace-honesty and pds-bl-manifest-writes-fails-open: does it still reproduce on origin/main, and what is the smallest honest fix?
The cheapest, densest cluster of "the owner is told something untrue" — likely one or two slices, not five.
import-error-honesty

Do the 25P02-masking rows still reproduce — pds-backlog-import-savepoint-honesty, pds-bl-clean-import-ungated-500, pds-bl-repull-into-populated-target-500? Wave 21 proved the 25P02 masked a 23505 unique violation from merge_upsert's PK-only ON CONFLICT arbiter. Has anything landed since that surfaces the FIRST real error?
An opaque 500 on a re-pull is the unattended owner's worst experience in the entire loop, and it sits squarely inside the wave's defect class.
collision-map

What is claimed, in flight, or open as a PR right now that touches our candidate surfaces — api/lib/barkpark/tasks/**, deploy/**, scripts/pds-*, internal/cli/cloud_*? List foreign claims on PDS rows, open PRs, and any epic-cycle worktree branches under .claude/worktrees.
Two other waves are running concurrently. Collision control is atomic bp claims, but a slice aimed at a file someone else holds is wasted before it starts.
charter-citation-smoke

git-show and READ FOR COVERAGE every charter decision this direction leans on: PDS-D31 (the one-export law), D74 (export/teardown lockstep), D100 (a FAIL is filed, not fixed), D105 (export cost), D207 (the spill), D214 (import deliberately unchanged), D279 and D280 (the 25P02 diagnosis). Report any decision cited as authority for something its text does not actually cover.
The arm-D phantom-D32 lesson: a real entry cited for authority it does not carry is a phantom wearing a number. This direction must not rest on one.
prior-art-search

Search Barkpark with bp search — it EXISTS; six surveyors once wrongly concluded otherwise, see pds-bl-bp-search-false-negative — for prior papers and tasks on honest-success, post-condition and vacuous-green doctrine, and specifically for how Truth-Grip wave 10 ran its tail triage. Name the method it used and the disposition vocabulary it settled on.
The wish explicitly asks for Truth-Grip wave 10's triage method. Copy a proven method rather than inventing a worse one.
owner-unattended-walk

Walk the owner's actual path today: bin/barkpark up on a fresh checkout, mint an admin token, pull a dataset, serve a media asset, re-pull. At each step, what is the owner TOLD, and is it true? Include the accuracy of docs/setup/personal-local.md (pds-bl-personal-local-doc-staleness, pds-bl-admin-token-mint-path).
The wave is judged by the unattended owner's experience, and nobody has yet written down what that experience actually is, end to end, in one pass.
test-seams

What test surfaces exist to PIN these fixes — the close and claim test files, workspace_bundle_test.exs's md5-parity tripwire, the CLI's ARGV-level harness, any deploy-script test? Which candidate fix currently has NO seam that could fail, and what would the smallest real seam be?
Charter law: a fix without a test that can fail is a claim, not a fix. This also guards the byte-identical full-fidelity rule if the import path is touched.
w21-housekeeping-verify

Verify by reading the ledger: pds-w21-diagnose-and-fire's criterion 6 merge-gate against #5547's merge commit 59818468e being an ancestor of origin/main; pds-w21-crown-collect-and-seal's criteria against the recorded seal; and the epic task's own claim state (epoch 4, worker null) plus its current wave_paper and wave_status fields.
Cheap and charter-assigned, but it must close on evidence rather than on the charter's say-so — the worktree premise in the very same paragraph was already stale.
quality-bar-gap

Against the Kinsta/Vercel bar the charter invokes: what does a comparable product tell its owner that Barkpark's PDS does not — deployment status and running version, an honest job and receipt history, a failure that names itself? Which of those gaps is closable by making an EXISTING surface honest rather than by building something new?
Keeps the wave ambitious without letting it drift into candidate B's new-capability trap, and distinguishes missing honesty from missing feature.

DIGEST — the survey, adjudicated

Phase: DIGEST complete. 17 surveyors reported; zero coverage deficit. The direction SURVIVES and is sharper: every named starting point was re-derived and three of the four moved. 12 verifiers now fly to PROVE the load-bearing claims by RUNNING things, not reading them. What the survey ESTABLISHED

The close gate is epoch-only, confirmed. check_fencing/2 has three clauses: epoch match → :ok, epoch mismatch → :fenced_off, and a bare `_ -> :ok` so a claimless task closes unconditionally. worker_id is WRITTEN to claim.closed_by and never COMPARED.

Of 2,064 recorded closes on the live guerrilla ledger, 36 have a live claim.worker ≠ closed_by and a further 40 were closed over a TTL-reaped lease by someone other than previous_worker — union 76 rows, 3.7%. The foreign closers are LEADS (oc-lead 29, cc-showcase 13), never CI, never the board UI. This IS the documented epic-cycle seal ritual, named in four charters.

Where the reports CONTRADICT the direction — four premise corrections
A premise that fails smoke is a finding, not a foundation. Four of the direction's own load-bearing premises moved.
The deploy defect is a box stuck one-or-more commits behind while everything reports success.

PARTLY. Re-measured live at digest time: guerrilla /status.json reports 0.2.25.1879 against origin/main's v0.2.25-1880 — ONE commit, i.e. a deploy in flight, not a stall. The earlier surveyor's five-commit gap was transient. Two further premises are outright wrong: instance-deploy.sh's exit 23 fires only for rollback modes (a real deploy queues, then exits 15), and every flip failure restores the Caddyfile, disables the new slot, resets the checkout and exits 14. The script's failure typing is GOOD.

The defect is NOT that the box silently stalls. It is that (a) the CLI prints ✓ deployed on an ssh exit code alone while the box ALREADY prints its live sha as unparsed log text, (b) the coalesce path exits 0 asserting 'already deployed healthy' from a state file it wrote itself, with no live probe it owns twice over, and (c) no anonymous observer can read the running COMMIT anywhere — /status.json carries version only, and capabilities withholds the sha from tier none. Re-scope to the OBSERVER gap.
The import receipt's em-dash is a fabrication bug worth a slice.

WORSE, and now proven by execution. The server sends `tables` as a MAP (workspace_bundle.ex:182 types it %{String.t() => non_neg_integer()}); the Go client decodes it into *int. The whole json.Unmarshal errors — but TotalRows decodes correctly to 13 in a run repro, and the `if err == nil` guard throws the working half away. So EVERY human-mode import prints 'Imported workspace X — — rows across — tables', always, and exits 0.
Not a wording fix. A ~6-line contract fix (map + independent per-field assignment) with a table-driven test that fails today. Also: importCounts, fetchOneBlob and putOneBlob have ZERO test coverage.
PDS-D100 licenses filing rather than fixing.

NO. D100 was git-shown verbatim: 'Every harness change lands in PREFLIGHT, before attempt 1. From attempt 1 onward the harness is FROZEN.' It is CLIMB-SCOPED. With the crown closed and no attempt running, D100 forbids this wave nothing and is inert.

This single ruling is the wave's largest lever. 58 of the 133 open rows name ONLY scripts/pds-* harness files, and the charter groups six of them at :2511-2513 under 'FILED, NOT BUILT (the freeze forbids touching the instrument)'. With the freeze inert, that family gets ONE adjudication — unpark with an owner, or park permanently because the instrument retires with the crown — instead of 58.
PDS-D207 authorises the constant-memory packing; PDS-D214 licenses leaving import in memory.

BOTH mis-citations. D207 rules on byte-identity vs member-level equivalence and the four add-by-path conditions; it never mentions constant memory — that ruling is D199 + D204. archive.ex's own moduledoc already carries the wrong number. And D214's out-of-scope call survives, in its own words, only because 'the scratch target runs on the LOCAL 16 GB Mac, never on guerrilla, with no concurrent live traffic and no lock-free public route' — four conditions an unattended owner's box negates.

Cite D199+D204 for delivery shape, D207 only for the identity gate, and fix archive.ex's moduledoc as a one-line honesty item. Treat D214 as an EXPIRED deferral to re-adjudicate, never as a standing licence.

The Direction — SUCCESS MUST BE OBSERVABLE
One law, proposed for the charter, and every slice is an instance of it:

No Barkpark verb may report success on an exit code alone. Every success claim must be backed by a post-condition READ of the state it claims to have produced — and any claim it cannot back must say so in the same breath. A green that cannot fail is not a green.

This is the repo's own agent doctrine — distrust vacuous green, verify STATE not exit codes, truth-authority level 1 is the running system — made EXECUTABLE IN THE PRODUCT rather than practised only by agents. That is exactly what separates a watched dev loop from an unattended one: a supervising lead re-derives every claim by hand; an owner cannot, so the box must do it, and must be loud when it cannot.

What the finished experience feels like. The owner deploys and the thing that says SUCCESS is the box's own advanced HEAD, not a CI conclusion. A close on the ledger means the worker who held the claim finished the criteria — or it says out loud, on the record, that it did not. An import receipt prints the rows it actually moved, not an em-dash. A second concurrent scratch target cannot silently strand the first. Four named starting points, to be RE-DERIVED and not trusted: pds-bl-deploy-success-without-advance, pds-bl-scratch-pointer-concurrency, pds-bl-close-holder-and-criteria-gate, pds-bl-streaming-workspace-export. Plus: triage the ~130 rows the way Truth-Grip wave 10 triaged its tail — adjudicate by CONTENT against main, close what is already fixed, park what is genuinely deferred WITH a durable reason, leave the rest open with a named owner. Do NOT re-fire the crown. Do NOT invent a new capability to avoid finishing the ones that exist.

The Direction — SUCCESS MUST BE OBSERVABLE

One law, proposed for the charter, and every slice is an instance of it:

The proposed law No Barkpark verb may report success on an exit code alone. Every success claim must be backed by a post-condition READ of the state it claims to have produced — and any claim it cannot back must say so in the same breath. A green that cannot fail is not a green.

This is the repo's own agent doctrine — distrust vacuous green, verify STATE not exit codes, truth-authority level 1 is the running system — made EXECUTABLE IN THE PRODUCT rather than practised only by agents. That is exactly what separates a watched dev loop from an unattended one: a supervising lead re-derives every claim by hand; an owner cannot, so the box must do it, and must be loud when it cannot.

What the finished experience feels like. The owner deploys and the thing that says SUCCESS is the box's own advanced HEAD, not a CI conclusion. A close on the ledger means the worker who held the claim finished the criteria — or it says out loud, on the record, that it did not. An import receipt prints the rows it actually moved, not an em-dash. A second concurrent scratch target cannot silently strand the first. An export route refuses work it cannot serve instead of dying trying. Nothing new is invented: four or five existing surfaces stop lying.

What the ground truth already changed

Premise smoke, run against origin/main @ fe1e4501a BEFORE any direction was committed. Three of the wish's own premises moved:

The first row is the argument for the triage track in miniature: one of the four named starting points was already fixed by a prior wave, and the ledger did not know. Triage here is not bookkeeping. It is what stops this wave rebuilding what main already has.

The Direction Debate

Three candidates were developed far enough to be attacked.

The sharpest attack found on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it:

ATTACK — the close gate can break the fleet that is running it A strict holder fence on bp task close would break the epic-cycle's own workflow. The charter says in plain text "PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge)", and wave 21 was sealed by a LEAD closing a builder's task. Two other waves and ~110 agents are on the ledger RIGHT NOW, some on older CLI builds. A criteria gate would additionally refuse legitimate closes — cancelled rows, and criteria the charter itself marks unmeasurable by design (pds-bl-reclimb-criterion4-unmeasurable-by-design). Shipped naively, this slice is an outage.

ABSORPTION, and it makes the slice better rather than smaller: the gate is LOUD, not CLOSED. A holder mismatch does not refuse — it demands an explicit, recorded override (a named actor and a reason written into the close event), so a lead close stays legal and becomes AUDITABLE for the first time. A done close with unmet criteria likewise requires an explicit accept-unmet carrying a reason, while cancelled and blocked lifecycles are untouched. And the default-on question is not settled by taste: a surveyor MEASURES how many real closes in the live task.closed event history had worker != holder before anything is gated. That is survey assignment 1, and it is the wave's single highest-leverage unknown.

Two lesser attacks and their answers. (1) "Triaging 130 rows is bureaucracy that fixes nothing." The streaming-export finding above already refutes it; and triage is surveyor and verifier fan-out — cheap, parallel — while builders spend only on defects. Every row must land in exactly one of: CLOSED with the commit that fixed it, PARKED with a durable reason and a named reopen trigger, or OPEN with a named owner and a size. (2) "Deploy honesty lives in .github/workflows, which is fenced to the concurrent Honest Gates wave." Correct, and the fence is respected — the honest fix belongs on the BOX side anyway, because the box's own advanced HEAD is the fact and a CI conclusion is at best hearsay. It lands in deploy/instance-deploy.sh plus a read path, never in the workflow file.

Priorities for this wave

Hard constraints this wave inherits No crown re-fire. Fable is unavailable (spend limit) — every joint runs Opus, and no dispatch may select fable. Keep off .github/workflows/** and the hg-* ledger namespace (concurrent Honest Gates wave) and tooling/grip/** (Truth-Grip refire); collision control is atomic bp claims. Main carries two standing reds — Format (advisory) and Sobelow — that are NOT ours. Guerrilla writes are degraded to 15-33s under concurrent load: NEVER conclude a ledger write failed without RE-READING the published state, which is, fittingly, this wave's own law applied to itself.

The Survey Plan — 17 assignments

Width now buys precise depth later. Each assignment is one Opus surveyor at medium effort. Every load-bearing assumption the stress-test surfaced appears below as a question.

Housekeeping ledger for this wave

Next append DIGEST appends the survey digest and the verify plan HERE, before any verifier flies. DECIDE then appends the decisions and the wave plan, before any builder flies. REVIEW closes the story as the debrief. This Paper is the wave's living story: Fable phases own it, workers write their own bp tasks and never this Paper.

DIGEST — the survey, adjudicated

Where this wave stands Phase: DIGEST complete. 17 surveyors reported; zero coverage deficit. The direction SURVIVES and is sharper: every named starting point was re-derived and three of the four moved. 12 verifiers now fly to PROVE the load-bearing claims by RUNNING things, not reading them. No builder flies until they land. Fable is unavailable this wave (spend limit) — the entire verify fleet is Opus.

Re-measured at digest time against origin/main @ 071d228d7 (main moved from fe1e4501a during the survey; every finding below was re-checked against the new head where it mattered).

What the survey ESTABLISHED

Six things are now settled with file:line or live-data evidence and should not be re-litigated.

Where the reports CONTRADICT the direction — four premise corrections

A premise that fails smoke is a finding, not a foundation. Four of the direction's own load-bearing premises moved.

The housekeeping the charter assigned is ALREADY DONE

Three surveyors adjudicated it independently and agree. Record it; do not spend a slice on it.

The triage corpus, counted honestly

The '~130 rows' figure is right and every simpler lens is wrong. Full BFS of task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5: 231 nodes, tree exactly two levels deep, 133 open descendants (129 open + 3 considering + 1 blocked), of which 82 are direct children and 51 are grandchildren. An id-prefix lens sees 131 and a direct-children lens sees 82 — the Truth-Grip D110 trap, reproduced. Zero of the 133 carry a claim.

Method is inherited whole from Truth-Grip wave 10, whose committed recipe is tooling/grip/ledger/tgw9-s4-tail-disposition-2026-07-27.recipe.md: two-lens blocking set, read every row individually, close by CONTENT never ancestry, leaves only, verify by RE-READ. And its failure is inherited as a warning: wave 10 claimed 45 parks each carried a reason, and 0 of 46 considering rows actually had a non-empty content.engagement.note. The mechanism worked; nobody looked. This wave's triage carries a criterion of the shape 'N rows disposed → N rows re-read → N non-empty reason fields, command pasted' — the wave's own law applied to its own bookkeeping.

Coverage map — what was checked, and what was NOT

Absences are decisions-in-waiting. These are the corners no surveyor reached, distilled from the 17 coverage tables.

The verify fleet — 12 assignments, all Opus, all proving by RUNNING

Fable is unavailable (monthly spend limit), so every assignment is Opus at medium. Each names what it will EXECUTE; reading is not proof for a claim of the form 'this passes', 'this endpoint returns X', or 'this test pins that behaviour'.

Next append DECIDE appends the decisions and the wave plan HERE, after the 12 verifiers land and before any builder flies. Fences honoured this wave: OFF .github/workflows/**, OFF hg-*, OFF tooling/grip/**. No crown re-fire. No new capability invented to avoid finishing one that exists.

Verification — what the deep round proved by RUN

Twelve Opus verifiers flew; every one reported (zero coverage deficit in both the survey and the verify round). Verdicts are ordered by how much they moved the plan. Trust proofs over facts over prose — every row below is backed by output that was actually produced, not by a reading.

Premise corrections the wave absorbed

Six inherited premises failed smoke or were re-measured into a different shape. Each one would have cost a builder if it had reached them unchallenged.

Coverage — including the not-founds

Both rounds reported in full: no survey agent and no verifier went missing. The verifiers' most useful negatives: there is NO dedicated test file for workspace_bundle/archive.ex (the import slice must land its fail-before inside the 30-test workspace_bundle_test.exs); NO test anywhere asserts holder identity on close; NO test file exists for the scratch pointer at all; NO concurrency primitive exists anywhere in api/lib/barkpark_web, so PDS-D31's one-export law is enforced nowhere in the product; and docs/api-v1.md does not document /v1/data/counts at all, so that criterion is an ADD. Three corners were deliberately left open and are recorded here rather than papered over: mutation_events carries the closer server-side but no read surface exposes it, so close-time refusability cannot be measured from published state; whether the compactor preserves claim.previous_worker is unverified, and a compacted row could turn a legal self-resume into an override on the record; and the Tickets/OTP-28 local failure (27 of 53) is undiagnosed and out of every lane.

Decisions — PDS-D287 through PDS-D304

Each is written in full in .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md (commit 1cb2e4883). The charter is the epic's memory; this table is the wave's index into it.

The wave plan — 8 slices, 7 in round 1

Three tracks, cut so that no two slices touch the same region of a file. Every slice is opus at medium: Fable 5 is unavailable this run (monthly spend limit), and a fable-selecting dispatch would silently lose the slice.

HIGH-FLIP-RISK: pds-w22-close-holder-criteria-honesty. The flip-prone judgment is the holder-gate semantics — whether a foreign close is refused or recorded, and whether the gate may be described as authorization at all. It cannot: worker_id is a client-supplied body param. The wave reviewer must re-derive that judgment INDEPENDENTLY rather than re-read the builder's reasoning, and a genuinely second reviewer is warranted before merge — a manual lead step, since this workflow spawns exactly one. Phase: DECIDE complete, 7 builders about to fly. NO crown re-fire. NO fable anywhere. Fences honoured: OFF .github/workflows/**, hg-*, tooling/grip/** except this run's own re-derivation rows.

DEBRIEF — what wave 22 actually shipped

Reviewed by one Fable in its own worktree: every green slice read as a full diff against its merge-base, every slice gate re-run on the final branch, every fix applied in place rather than reported. Grade B+. Seven slices built, seven branches pushed, PRs #6420 through #6426 open; the charter entry rides #6427. The lead merges.

The wish was that the product stop reporting success while being wrong, in an owner's hands, unattended. Five product surfaces stopped lying and every one of them was proven by MUTATION rather than by reading: the close ledger, the deploy slot stamp and the harness that polices it, the public running-commit read path, the import receipt and the blob byte-verify, and the capabilities writes bit plus a counts perspective that was being silently discarded. That is the wish moved forward, honestly.

Per slice — final branch, verdict, what the lead must know

The finding that changes the grade — 19 adjudications evaporated

PDS-D298 was written because Truth-Grip wave 10 claimed 45 park reasons and had 0 of 46. Wave 22 carried that law into its own bookkeeping and both triage slices re-read what they wrote. An independent census at review time, over the whole epic scope of 265 rows, measured this:

bp task stage --note reports success, lands the lifecycle flip, and the engagement map is silently dropped afterwards. The 8 parks that survived did so only because the harness/crown slice ALSO wrote content.disposition_reason. All 31 rows carry a content.github key, consistent with a reconciler rebuilding content wholesale. The reviewer re-parked all 19 lost rows into disposition_reason and re-read 19 of 19 — but their ORIGINAL adjudication text is unrecoverable, and that is a real loss, not a bookkeeping nit: those were the reasons a future wave would have read before deciding whether the park still holds.

DATED CORRECTION to the DIGEST section 'The housekeeping the charter assigned is ALREADY DONE' and to the D298 proof standard as stated at DECIDE (2026-07-28): the standard is sound and the slices obeyed it, but a re-read at write time is NOT a durability proof. The proof obligation is a re-read after a settle window measured in HOURS, or a write to a field known to survive. Recorded as PDS-D306. pds-bl-stage-note-evaporates was closed as a duplicate into pds-bl-park-note-evaporates, which now carries the census.

What the lead must know before merging

MERGE ORDER MATTERS. api/** auto-deploys on merge, so the moment #6420 lands, guerrilla enforces the close holder gate. Every wave-22 slice row's last holder is its BUILDER, so a lead sealing them is a foreign close: 409 not_holder unless the close carries --set holder_override="<why>". A close over a still-unmet criterion needs --set criteria_override="<why>". Merge #6420 LAST, or seal the other six rows before it deploys. Recorded as PDS-D305.

MERGE-GATED CRITERIA the lead closes on merge: every slice row sits at n-1 of n (or 6 of 8 for the close slice), with the final criterion being the PR merge. All seven rows read lifecycle open with no claim — their leases were TTL-reaped mid-run — so the reviewer stamped each with a disposition naming the branch, the PR and the re-run gate, otherwise the board reads them as never started.

TWO JUDGMENT CALLS a lead may want to overturn. First, D289's criteria gate measures the doc AS READ, which re-specifies what a close MEANS for every caller in the system — the documented seal ritual bp task close --set 'criteria:=[…]' now requires stamp-as-you-go or a recorded reason. The builder itself argued the narrower version is defensible. Second, the counts refusal reuses the registered 400 code malformed rather than a purpose-named code, because a new code needs a Content.Errors registration and an openapi enum regen.

Ledger audit

137 rows adjudicated across the two triage slices; the epic scope now reads 124 open, 31 considering, 84 done, 24 cancelled, 1 blocked. Every done row carries a close_reason (84 of 84). 98 of the 124 open rows carry a disposition_reason with a named owner. The two w21 housekeeping rows are done 7/7 and 6/6 and were SELF closes, exactly as D300 said. No task outside this wave's scope was touched except the two duplicate defect rows, which were collapsed to one.

Reviewer's ledger fixes: 19 evaporated parks re-parked into disposition_reason (19/19 verified by re-read); pds-bl-stage-note-evaporates closed as a duplicate into pds-bl-park-note-evaporates and the survivor sharpened with the census; all seven built slice rows stamped with a disposition naming branch, PR, gate and the holder_override warning; the epic task's wave_status and wave_paper stamped. One write reproduced the large-task ceiling — a ~1 KB disposition_reason published 422 validation_failed where ~260 B published first try, which is a second independent witness for pds-bl-large-task-write-500 (PDS-D308).

The grade, earned

B+. What is genuinely strong: every code slice closed a REAL defect that was proven to exist by running the broken thing first, and four of the five closed it with a test that fails against main. The deploy slice's ordering discipline — fix the harness that cannot fail before touching the thing it polices — is the wave's best work and the clearest expression of its own law. Builders' self-reviews were unusually honest: three of them named the exact hole a reviewer would find, and two of them argued against their own brief and were right to.

What falls short, and why it is not an A. The close slice shipped a gate that could not be escaped over the wire and left four out-of-fence tests red; the manifest slice left a fifth. Either would have failed the Elixir gate on merge, which means two of seven slices were not actually mergeable as delivered — the reviewer, not the builder, made them so. The triage moved 137 rows but fixed nothing: 31 of the 36 removals are parks, and 19 of those parks then lost the very reason that made them a disposition rather than a silence. A wave whose subject is 'success must be observable' losing 61 percent of its own adjudications is the sharpest possible self-indictment, and it is why this is not an A-. And of the four correctness defects the wish named by name, one — pds-bl-scratch-pointer-concurrency — was taken by no slice at all.

What is NOT wrong with it: there is no bloat here. No slice invented a capability to avoid finishing an existing one, nobody re-fired the crown, and no slice is padded. The diffs are small and the comments earn their lines.

What the next wave should take

Dispatch order first: merge round 1, then pds-w22-deploy-readback the moment #6422 is on main — it reads the /status.json commit field that PR adds, and it is the slice that finally makes bp cloud deploy prove the box advanced instead of printing a checkmark on an ssh exit code. That is the wish's flagship and it is one merge away.

Then, in order: fix pds-bl-park-note-evaporates, because the ledger is this epic's spine and a wave cannot triage onto a surface that forgets; take pds-bl-scratch-pointer-concurrency defect 1, which the wish named and nobody took; and take the two rows the triage itself nominated as the strongest remaining report-success-while-wrong shapes, pds-bl-w16-full-meta-permissive-default and pds-bl-w16-failed-refetch-destroys-parked-bundle, plus pds-bl-bounded-import-unpack. All are mutation-provable without any fire. Do not re-fire the crown.

One independent second reviewer is owed before #6420 merges, on the holder-gate semantics and on whether D289's doc-as-read criteria gate is wider than the defect it closes. This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a manual lead step.
